A_target.statement:
Let $f, g: X \to Y$ be mappings, and $\sim$ the smallest [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence relation]] on $Y$ with $\map f x \sim \map g x$ for all $x \in X$.
Then the [[Definition:Quotient Mapping|quotient map]] $q: Y \to Y / \sim$ is a [[Definition:Coequalizer|coequalizer]] of $f$ and $g$ in $\mathbf {Set}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $Y$.
Then mappings $Y / \sim \to Z$ correspond to mappings $Y \to Z$ which are constant on equivalence classes.

substitutions.the equivalence relation: the one generated by the pairs (f(x), g(x))

derived.factorization through the quotient: the universal property of the coequalizer

object_map.reformulation: Collapse exactly what f and g force to be equal, and check universality via the kernel relation of a test map.

validity_conditions: The kernel relation of any mapping is an equivalence relation, which is what allows minimality to be used.
In groups or rings, the generated normal subgroup or ideal plays the role of the generated equivalence relation.
proof_plan:
Let $h: Y \to Z$ with $h \circ f = h \circ g$.
The relation $\map h y = \map h {y'}$ is an equivalence relation containing every pair $\tuple {\map f x, \map g x}$.

By minimality, $\sim$ is contained in it, so $h$ is constant on $\sim$-classes.
By the source result, there is a unique $\bar h$ with $\bar h \circ q = h$.

Hence $q$ is a coequalizer of $f$ and $g$.
{{qed}}
